reviews.review: Whoever bought this game, You seriously need to go check your self in a Mental hospital, because this game definitely is not worth more than 5 bucks.

[h1] 5/10 - "Fun, but abandoned far too quickly" [/h1]

Haven't finished the game yet but it'd be much higher on my list of recommendations if it weren't for the game breaking bugs that lock you out of entire sections of the game. 
Without getting into spoilers the very first area you go is randomized from 3 potential areas which means you likely won't start in the same world as your friends which I found VERY interesting as this sucked me into the world more, however, the world I happened to start off in has a bug with it's main npc that hard locks you out of the last portion of that world entirely and upon researching it seems this is a bug from launch that never got patched properly so even after all those dlc packs they never ensured the base game was working fine which is a shame. I'm not one to tell them how to do their job, but this should've been properly patched. I've tried all the recommended methods and my only recourse for this predicament to re-roll my entire campaign but I would have no way of knowing if that'll work unless I got to that point in the story again. Either that or starting a new character. One of the best parts of the original was all the different items you'd have to choose from with npcs so you'd have several things to look forward to that you missed out on with NG+, I have to admit though that thanks to such a troubling experience in the second game (from the very first world no less) I am entirely enthused to even attempt navigating this game breaking conundrum to even finish the game once. This is but one bug unfortunately, I have heard there are more though I wouldn't know since I can't progress, with that said however I'll dig into the game itself, I will try to keep it spoiler free. 

[h3] Combat [/h3]
I enjoyed the combat from the portion I've played, I got to see my sibling's first world and it's enemies and even take some items back from it which helped me a fair amount but it seems like they didn't tamper with what made the first games mix of gunplay + melee so great, rather, they expanded on it some interesting ways with classes and cross classing which in essence just provide you with more abilities for your arsenal and don't lock you into a particular playstyle which I'm grateful for. The modifications work identically to the first game when you attach them to your weapons, you're free to swap them about on your weapons as you please and decide which ones work best for your chosen playstyle. All in all good marks. Enemies aren't terribly spongey and solo'ing is a nice experience however this game and it's bosses are very much designed to be played with a buddy or two so don't beat yourself up for dying every now and again if you're going the solo route.  

[h3] Story [/h3]
Without delving into the whole thing I just want to note I'm fond of the few elements from the first game they chose to weave back into this games plot, however it's been pretty bland and the environments remained the most interesting aspects to me. I can't even remember any of the story beats when I picked it back up before writing this so take that as you will. Also I would've loved less cutscenes and dialogue that lock me in place for an extended period of time, "show don't tell" seems to be a writing rule they sorta ignored. 

[h3] Critiques [/h3]
The game isn't fresh enough on my mind for me to remember absolutely everything, there are more in-depth reviews for that sorta thing, but here's what I remember bugging me: [u] 1. Can't edit character after initial creation [/u] - Seriously? I realize this isn't the best first example and has very little to do with the actual game, but what are even doing, even Bungie eventually caved and let us edit our guardians in Destiny 2 and FromSoft learned gave us the option to edit our characters in Elden Ring, so what's the excuse here? I don't want to linger on something so trivial, but I had to learn how to dig into the files to subvert this design choice and I'm really not fond of it. [u] 2. Bigger doesn't mean better. The maps [/u] - I promise I'm not being overly critical here, most of the areas have a nice balance to them but they're also terribly empty, enemy variety felt good enough to encompass these regions but I had a few moments when backtracking for loot where I wished I could just teleport to small waypoints as opposed to hoofing it the whole way again. It's not overbearing and maybe it has something to do with the procedural aspects of the game, but it seems like it could've used a little more refinement. Peppering in mini bosses or significant points of interest to read up on the locale and it's history might've fixed this for me I think. 

[h3] Conclusion [/h3]
I hate to disappoint for covering so little, I might update this in the future if I remember anything else or need to clarify certain points, perhaps I'll even be able to get past that hard lock bug and finish the game, but for now I've only to say the game is fun for what is is for a time but I hold firm in my stance that the game was left behind far too soon from the devs, there are a fair number of things that still need patched and I don't see myself purchasing their future titles if they intend on making a habit of leaving such issues unattended. I enjoyed the time I've spent in-game but wish it'd be a little more polished.

A very fun co-op focused game with interesting cooperative mechanics, puzzles, and boss fights. The boss fights are spectacles and impressive to play the first time around, and the environments are fairly interesting too. The story is the weakest point, it is at times both convoluted and incoherent, while also being very simple at its core. Definitely a focus on the gameplay kind of game. It's less of a 'dark souls with guns' from the first game, but more of a co-op action game with light souls inspired mechanics. Some of the systems are kind of interesting, but end up just being incremental stat increases which is a shame. I do have issue with how they did the world/adventure system, I would have much preferred a more traditional or even linear map progression system rather than relying on RNG to reroll maps to experience everything, as some of the maps and questlines are actually pretty interesting yet no one will experience them on their first playthrough. Overall, it's a fun co op game but is just okay in solo.
